Let
\[
A=k[u,v,w,s].
\]
The relations say that \(R\) is the algebra generated by \(A\) and commuting operators \(X,Y\), where
\[
Xa=aX+D(a),\qquad Ya=aY+E(a)\qquad(a\in A),
\]
for the \(k\)-derivations
\[
D(u)=0,\ D(v)=u,\ D(w)=0,\ D(s)=(1-u)w+2uv+u^3,
\]
\[
E(u)=0,\ E(v)=u^2,\ E(w)=u,\ E(s)=u(1-u)w+(1-u+2u^2)v+u^2+u^4.
\]

First, any central element has no \(X\) or \(Y\) terms. Indeed, write
\[
P=\sum c_{ij}X^iY^j,\qquad c_{ij}\in A.
\]
Since \([Y,w]=u\) and \([X,w]=0\),
\[
[Y^j,w]=juY^{j-1}.
\]
Looking at the highest \(Y\)-degree in \([P,w]\) forces all terms with \(j>0\) to vanish. Thus \(P\in A[X]\). Similarly, since \([X,v]=u\),
\[
[X^i,v]=iuX^{i-1},
\]
so centrality with \(v\) forces all terms with \(i>0\) to vanish. Hence
\[
Z(R)=A^{D,E}:=\{f\in A:D(f)=E(f)=0\}.
\]

Now compute the common invariants. Over \(K=k(u)\), define
\[
Q=us-\bigl((1-u)w+u^3\bigr)v-uv^2.
\]
A direct calculation gives \(D(Q)=0\), and since \(D(w)=0\), we have
\[
K[v,w,s]^D=K[w,Q].
\]
On this kernel,
\[
E(w)=u,\qquad E(Q)=u^3.
\]
Therefore the \(E\)-invariant combination is
\[
T:=Q-u^2w
=us-(1-u)wv-u^3v-uv^2-u^2w.
\]
Indeed,
\[
D(T)=0,\qquad E(T)=0.
\]
Thus over \(k(u)\),
\[
K[v,w,s]^{D,E}=K[T].
\]

Finally, \(T\in k[u,v,w,s]\), and \(T\) is primitive as a polynomial over \(k[u]\); reducing modulo any irreducible polynomial in \(k[u]\) still gives a nonconstant polynomial in \(v,w,s\). Hence
\[
k(u)[T]\cap k[u,v,w,s]=k[u,T].
\]

Therefore
\[
\boxed{
Z(R)=k\!\left[u,\ us-(1-u)wv-u^3v-uv^2-u^2w\right].
}
\]
